subject: Request: proportional exit rights for repeat latency breaches
messages:
From: Saira Khan <saira.khan@medtechinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.co le@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: MedTech Inc Legal <legal@medtechinc.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: proportional exit rights for repeat latency breaches

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we take internal procurement through our security and legal review, a couple of redlines are blocking us from finalizing the SOW/SLA. The core ask is: beyond credits, MedTech needs proportional exit rights and a fee-at-risk mechanism if latency/uplift issues repeat. Specifically: 

- If Redwood experiences Severity 1 latency incidents (as defined in the SLA) 3 times within a rolling 90-day window, MedTech wants a right to terminate for convenience with a 60-day notice and a partial buyout equal to remaining committed fees for the next 3 months.
- For repeat Severity 2 incidents (5+ impacting windows in 30 days) we want an escrowed fee-at-risk equal to 10% of monthly committed spend, releasable back to Redwood if performance returns to SLOs for 60 days; refundable to MedTech after a material failure.
- We also want a simple liquidated damages schedule for single-event Severity 1 outages: $X per hour beyond the first hour, capped at 100% of the monthly committed fee. (See attached spreadsheet with suggested figures.)

We're flexible on cure windows but need contractual certainty beyond credits; credits alone are not sufficient for our compliance/risk team. Can you tell me whether Redwood can accept proportional exit rights and an escrowed fee-at-risk, or propose a commercial alternative? If needed, legal can hop on a quick call.

Attachments: medtech-proposed-penalties-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Saira
Director, Cloud Platform
MedTech Inc
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Saira Khan <saira.khan@medtechinc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: proportional exit rights for repeat latency breaches

Hi Saira — thanks for the clear write-up and the spreadsheet. We appreciate the urgency and the sensitivity for MedTech's compliance team. High level: we understand the need for stronger levers than credits, but we have some constraints on termination/buyout language and escrow mechanics we need to reconcile internally.

Proposed next steps from our side: 
- We can consider a staged fee-at-risk held in escrow (monthly accrual), but we typically cap buyout exposure to a fixed multiple of monthly committed spend and require a mutual review process before releasing funds.
- For termination: we prefer a remediation-first path (cure periods, rollback to a fallback model) and would propose termination only after (a) 3 uncured Severity 1 incidents in 90 days OR (b) a single Severity 1 outage >72 hours, with a capped buyout equal to 3 months of committed fees less any service credits paid.
- For single-event liquidated amounts, we don't accept open-ended per-hour damages; we can offer a defined hourly credit multiplier up to a contractual cap as above.

Looping Karthik and Ben to confirm technical remediation guarantees and whether the escrow cadence your team proposes is operationally workable. Happy to set a 30m call with legal to align on acceptable language.

—Marissa
SVP, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Marissa — quick internal notes on the proposed commercial unpack: 

- Operational feasibility: we can instrument a rolling-90d incident counter and export audit logs to validate breach counts; we should offer monthly incident reports to MedTech.
- Escrow mechanics: ops prefers monthly accrual into a third-party escrow (our finance team can manage), releasable on a mutually agreed remediation signoff. But we need a clear definition of remediation and a short mutual review window (10 business days) to avoid disputed releases.
- Cure and fallback: we should push for automatic fallback to a pinned older model and a 72-hour cure before termination is exercised. For continuous availability customers we can propose a separate buyout schedule but capped at 3x monthly spend.

If we accept escrow + termination after 3 uncured S1s (90d), we should insist on: 1) a maximum aggregate liability cap tied to committed spend, and 2) a requirement that MedTech attempt a structured remediation (canary rollback, request for increased capacity) before tapping escrow.

I can draft a short clause for legal to review if you want.

—Karthik
Director, Enterprise Solutions

On Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 11:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Hi Saira — thanks for the clear write-up and the spreadsheet...
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Saira Khan <saira.khan@medtechinc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, MedTech Inc Legal <legal@medtechinc.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: proportional exit rights for repeat latency breaches

Saira — thanks for your patience. Ben and I reviewed the proposed numbers and Karthik's implementation notes. We want to propose concrete wording that balances MedTech's risk needs and Redwood's operational constraints: 

1) Escrowed fee-at-risk: 8% monthly accrual of committed spend into a neutral third-party escrow administered by finance. Funds accrue monthly and are only releasable to MedTech after either (a) a final uncured Severity 1 event as defined below, or (b) failure to meet a mutually agreed remediation plan within 30 days of the incident report. Release disputes follow an expedited 10-business-day dispute resolution timeline.

2) Termination right: MedTech may terminate for convenience with 60 days' notice after three verified, uncured Severity 1 incidents in a rolling 90-day window. The termination payment is capped at the lesser of (i) 3 months of committed fees or (ii) the escrowed balance at the time of termination, less any service credits already paid.

3) Single-event compensation: For Severity 1 outages lasting >1 hour, Redwood will provide credits at 2x the hourly pro rata of committed monthly fees for the first 24 hours, then 1x beyond that, capped at the same termination cap above. We cannot accept open-ended per-hour liquidated damages.

We believe the structure above gives MedTech faster recourse than credits alone while limiting Redwood's open liability. If MedTech confirms acceptance of the mechanism above we will route a redline to legal with the precise escrow admin language. Otherwise, we can schedule legal call this week.

Thanks,
Marissa

Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: proportional exit rights for repeat latency breaches

Marissa — thanks for the pragmatic proposal and for looping Ben and Karthik. We're close. A couple of follow-ups from legal: 

- Legal asks we bump the escrow accrual to 10% (from 8%) and allow for a one-time administrative release to Redwood if the root cause is demonstrated to be outside Redwood's control (force majeure style incidents).
- They also want a shorter dispute window (5 business days) to expedite fund releases.

Commercially, MedTech can accept the termination cap tied to escrow balance, but we need the 10% accrual and a slightly shorter cure (20 days) for remediation timelines. Are you able to accept 10% and the 20-day cure? If so, we'll sign off and route the redlines back to you.

Attachments: redlines-sla-6-30-27.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Saira
